o1.biggest_strength: Every ad set is judged on an attribution-adjusted, after-RTO profit line, and the plan gives a dated first move for Saturday. The retargeting geo holdout is a smart way to test whether retargeting adds orders at all.
o1.biggest_mistake: The 86%/72% attribution split is invented, and labels and numbers sometimes disagree: retargeting is marked 'Cut' but only halved. Committing just ₹4.1L of ₹5.6L, with zero scale calls, means it under-deploys budget even though stock and cash are fine.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Fix the retargeting label. Justify or simplify the 86% assumption. Add a short creative brief for the revived hook. Give the reserve a clearer path to ASC so the team spends most of the budget when costs recover.

o2.biggest_strength: The ₹282 safe line and ₹394 break-even line give the team a simple scale/hold/cut rule. It puts a rupee value of about ₹65k on the paused creator video. The women's age losses are broken out by band, and the creative brief uses Rohan's and Ananya's words. I checked the per-ad-set break-evens, profits and budget total, and they hold up.
o2.biggest_mistake: The main results table is on Meta's count, so it shows ASC at +₹30k when the store-count view is far worse. Scaling Catalog DPA at frequency 5.2 is a stretch.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Show a Shopify-adjusted profit column next to the Meta count. Hold Catalog DPA rather than scale it. Add a dated first-day checklist.

reason: Both did the math right and made the same core calls. Output 2 is clearer, ready to hand to my team, and includes a creative brief. Output 1's attribution rigour and holdout test are sharp, but it leaves budget unspent and its labels are messier.
